questions.stem: Which biological molecule serves as the main structural component of cell membranes?
questions.explanation: Phospholipids form the bilayer structure of cell membranes, with their hydrophilic heads facing outward and hydrophobic tails facing inward.

questions.stem: What is the storage polysaccharide found in plants?
questions.explanation: Starch is the main energy storage polysaccharide in plants, stored in structures such as starch grains in chloroplasts and storage organs like potato tubers.

questions.stem: What type of reaction breaks a polymer into its monomers?
questions.explanation: Hydrolysis reactions break polymers into monomers by adding water. This is the reverse of condensation reactions that build polymers.
Proteins contain nitrogen as part of their amino acid structure (in the amino group -NH2). Carbohydrates and lipids contain only carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen.

questions.stem: What is the role of enzymes in biological reactions?

options.text: They are used up during the reaction
They increase the temperature of reactions
They act as biological catalysts, lowering activation energy

questions.explanation: Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed up reactions by lowering the activation energy needed. They are not used up and can be reused.

questions.stem: Which molecule provides the most energy per gram?
questions.explanation: Lipids provide approximately 37 kJ per gram, which is roughly double the energy provided by carbohydrates (17 kJ per gram), making them the most energy-dense biological molecule.

questions.stem: What structural polysaccharide is found in plant cell walls?
questions.explanation: Cellulose is the structural polysaccharide found in plant cell walls. It is made of beta glucose monomers and forms strong, insoluble microfibrils that provide rigidity.
